title: Inventory and eligibility of Arc machines
what: Machines by status, operating system, region, manufacturer/model, and detected SQL Server.
crit: Informational: baseline for the other controls.
steps: Use the inventory as a baseline: status, OS, region, and detected SQL per machine.
Separate machines by environment (production, staging) and by workload before any automation.
how: No decision: this is the basis for prioritizing the other actions.
resultCriteria: INFO by design (inventory, not scored): counts Arc machines by connection status, OS and SQL detection; this inventory is the denominator for the other checks.

title: Arc service per environment type
what: Source of each machine (on-premises, VMware, SCVMM, AWS/GCP, OCI) and chosen service (Arc-enabled servers, multicloud connector, Arc VMware/SCVMM).
crit: Evidence: decision recorded per source.
steps: Record, for each source (physical, VMware, SCVMM, AWS/GCP, OCI), the chosen onboarding method.
how: Follow DEC-01: if VM lifecycle is needed, use Arc VMware/SCVMM; on AWS/GCP with automatic discovery, Multicloud connector; in other cases, Arc-enabled servers.
resultCriteria: PASS when the Arc service used for each environment type (servers, SQL Server, Kubernetes, VMware/SCVMM) is documented with an owner; WARN when only part of the environments is covered. TODO until the customer's documentary evidence is recorded.

title: Landing zone and resource organization
what: Management group, subscriptions, and resource groups per environment and region; platform separated from workloads.
crit: Evidence: approved design.
steps: Define management groups, subscriptions, and resource groups by environment and region; separate platform from workloads.
how: Use the same structure as the Azure landing zone; a resource group per environment/region simplifies RBAC, policy, and cost.
resultCriteria: PASS when Arc resources follow a documented landing zone (management group, subscription, resource group and naming standard); WARN when the design exists but is not applied to every Arc resource. TODO until the customer's documentary evidence is recorded.

title: Criticality profile (Tier 0/1/2)
what: Server classification and stricter controls for Tier 0.
crit: Evidence: list of servers per tier and controls per tier.
steps: Classify servers into Tier 0/1/2 and record the list.
Apply stricter controls to Tier 0 (no Run Command/SSH/WAC, minimal allowlist).
how: Tier 0 = controls identity or security (AD, PKI, backup, management tools). When in doubt, classify in the higher tier.
resultCriteria: PASS when every Arc machine has a documented tier (0/1/2) that drives controls; WARN when some machines have no tier; FAIL when Tier 0 assets are not identified. TODO until the customer's documentary evidence is recorded.

title: Metadata region and data residency
what: Region of each machine compared with the allowed regions (optional).
crit: WARN if any machine is outside the allowed regions; INFO without a list.
steps: Confirm the regions allowed by the customer data policy.
Move metadata to the allowed region: requires removing the machine and redoing its onboarding.
how: Machine metadata is stored in the region of the Arc resource. Change it only if there is a regulatory or contractual requirement.
docs: Data, replication and disaster recovery for Arc-enabled servers
Rename and migrate Arc-enabled servers across regions
resultCriteria: PARTIAL when the allowed-region/data-residency policy is not supplied (regions are only listed, so compliance cannot be concluded); WARN if any machine is outside the allowed regions; PASS when every machine is inside them.

title: Recommended tags (best practice)
what: Tags of each machine compared with the recommended list (optional).
crit: INFO when any recommended tag is missing; N/A without a list.
steps: Define the tag standard (optional) and enforce it with Azure Policy (inherit from the resource group or require at creation).
how: Tags are a best practice, not a requirement. Prioritize those that feed cost (costCenter) and operations (owner, patchWindow).
resultCriteria: INFO by design (best practice, not scored): counts machines missing at least one of the tags env, owner, criticality, costCenter, dataClassification and patchWindow.

title: Registered resource providers
what: Registration state per subscription.
crit: FAIL if HybridCompute, GuestConfiguration, or HybridConnectivity are not registered; WARN for the recommended ones.
steps: Register the required providers in each subscription: Microsoft.HybridCompute, Microsoft.GuestConfiguration, Microsoft.HybridConnectivity (and Microsoft.AzureArcData for SQL).
how: Mandatory when FAIL: without the providers, onboarding and extensions fail.
resultCriteria: PASS when every essential and recommended resource provider is Registered in all subscriptions in scope; FAIL when an essential provider is not registered in any subscription (onboarding and extensions fail without it).

title: Azure Policy and baseline assignments
what: Assignments in scope and enforcement mode.
crit: WARN if no assignment relates to Arc/security; reports those in DoNotEnforce.
steps: Assign the Arc security baseline and the onboarding policies (AMA, Defender, Machine Configuration) at the management group.
Review assignments in DoNotEnforce.
how: Start in audit mode (Audit/AuditIfNotExists) and only then enable DeployIfNotExists with a remediation task.
resultCriteria: INFO by design (inventory): lists the Azure Policy assignments that reach Arc machines and flags DoNotEnforce; the compliance outcome is scored in CHK-09.

title: Policy compliance on the machines
what: NonCompliant states grouped by assignment and definition.
crit: WARN if there is noncompliance.
steps: Open the noncompliant rules with the most machines and create a remediation task or a documented exception.
how: Fix security ones and those affecting the most machines first; exceptions only with an owner and a timeframe.
resultCriteria: WARN if there is noncompliance.

title: Privileged roles in scope
what: Owner, User Access Administrator, RBAC Administrator, and Contributor by principal type.
crit: WARN if there is direct Owner/UAA/RBAC Admin for a user.
steps: Remove direct Owner/User Access Administrator assignments from users; use groups.
Enable PIM (just-in-time activation) for privileged roles.
how: Permanent assignment to a user only for an emergency (break-glass) account, documented.
resultCriteria: WARN if there is direct Owner/UAA/RBAC Admin for a user.

title: Arc-specific roles
what: Azure Connected Machine Onboarding, Resource Administrator, and similar roles.
crit: WARN if the onboarding role is assigned to a user.
steps: Assign the onboarding role to a dedicated service principal, scoped to the target resource group.
how: Users must not keep the onboarding role after deployment.
resultCriteria: INFO by design (inventory): counts Arc-specific role assignments that reach Arc machines; privilege risk is scored in CHK-10.

title: Managed identity of the machines
what: Roles assigned to the managed identities of Arc machines.
crit: FAIL if there is a privileged role: the local administrator of the machine inherits this access in Azure.
steps: Remove privileged roles (Owner, Contributor, Administrator) from the managed identities of Arc machines.
Grant only the minimum role for the specific resource (for example, read access to a Key Vault).
how: Anyone who is a local administrator of the machine can use its identity: treat it as access by that administrator in Azure.
resultCriteria: PASS when no Arc machine managed identity holds a role assignment in scope; non-PASS when any machine identity holds one and least privilege must be reviewed.

title: Identity model, PIM, and access review
what: Entra groups by function, PIM/JIT for privileged roles, and periodic review.
crit: Evidence: group matrix and PIM configuration.
steps: Define Entra groups by role, PIM for privileged roles, and quarterly access reviews.
how: Follow least privilege: Arc-specific roles before Contributor.
resultCriteria: PASS when privileged access to the Arc scope uses groups with PIM (eligible, time-bound) and periodic access reviews are evidenced; WARN when only part is in place; FAIL when standing privileged access exists without review. TODO until the customer's documentary evidence is recorded.

title: Onboarding secrets and credentials
what: Dedicated service principal, secret with expiration stored in a vault, no secrets in scripts; managed identity when possible.
crit: Evidence: rotation procedure and storage location.
steps: Use a dedicated service principal for onboarding, with a short-lived secret stored in a vault.
Remove secrets from scripts and rotate them after each wave.
Service principal with Azure Connected Machine Onboarding only; for GPO deployment, restrict the shared folder and remove the GPO and the scheduled task when done.
how: If the secret appeared in a script or repository, rotate it immediately.
resultCriteria: PASS when onboarding credentials use a dedicated service principal with the Azure Connected Machine Onboarding role, stored in a vault, with expiry and rotation; FAIL when secrets are embedded in scripts or never expire. TODO until the customer's documentary evidence is recorded.

title: Key Vaults
what: Public access, purge protection, and RBAC permission model.
crit: WARN for a definite baseline gap; PARTIAL when a required property is null/absent and no PASS/WARN conclusion is possible. Null/absent is never treated as false.
steps: Enable purge protection and the RBAC permission model; restrict public access on the vaults used by Arc.
how: Prioritize the vaults that store onboarding secrets or server certificates.
resultCriteria: WARN for a definite baseline gap; PARTIAL when a required property is null/absent and no PASS/WARN conclusion is possible. Null/absent is never treated as false.

title: Cross-subscription scenarios
what: Private Endpoint, Private Link Scope, and ExpressRoute across subscriptions; approval of Pending connections.
crit: Evidence: RBAC on both sides and approval flow.
steps: Map dependencies between subscriptions (Private Link Scope, DNS, workspace, DCR) and the RBAC required on both sides.
how: Shared resources (hub, SOC) must be in the collection scope or have a defined owner.
resultCriteria: PASS when cross-subscription/cross-tenant scenarios (shared workspaces, Private Link Scopes, delegated access) are documented with owners and access boundaries; WARN when they exist but are not documented. TODO until the customer's documentary evidence is recorded.

title: Connectivity model in use
what: Machines via Private Link, via proxy, Arc gateways, and public endpoints.
crit: Informational: compare with the connectivity decision.
steps: Compare the model in use with the connectivity decision (DEC-05 to DEC-08) and record the exceptions.
how: Private (Private Link) when policy requires traffic without internet; Arc gateway to reduce FQDNs; explicit proxy when it is already the corporate standard.
resultCriteria: INFO by design (inventory): reports the connectivity model per machine (Private Link, proxy, Arc gateway or public endpoints); security decisions are scored in CHK-18, CHK-19 and CHK-20.

title: Private Link Scope public access
what: publicNetworkAccess of each Azure Arc Private Link Scope.
crit: FAIL if any scope allows public access; N/A without Private Link.
steps: Disable public access on the Private Link Scope that should be private.
how: If machines still depend on public access, migrate them first and then disable it.
resultCriteria: N/A when no Azure Arc Private Link Scope exists in scope; otherwise PASS when every Private Link Scope denies public network access and FAIL when any allows it.

title: Arc private DNS
what: privatelink.his.arc.azure.com and privatelink.guestconfiguration.azure.com zones and DNS Private Resolver.
crit: WARN if there is Private Link without the zones in scope (they may be in the hub).
steps: Create or link the privatelink.his.arc.azure.com and privatelink.guestconfiguration.azure.com zones and the on-premises DNS forwarding.
how: If the zones are in the hub, include the hub subscription in the collection to confirm.
resultCriteria: N/A without an Azure Arc Private Link Scope; otherwise PASS when privatelink.his.arc.azure.com and privatelink.guestconfiguration.azure.com are present in the collected scope, and WARN when either zone is missing (the zone may be hosted in a hub subscription or on-premises DNS outside the collected scope).

title: Connectivity decision and network allowances
what: Chosen model (private, Arc gateway, explicit proxy, or direct), FQDN/Service Tags allowlist, Entra ID and ARM allowed, no TLS inspection on the gateway.
crit: Evidence: approved decision and firewall/proxy rules.
steps: Approve the connectivity model and the allowed endpoints (FQDNs or Service Tags), with no TLS inspection of agent traffic.
how: Entra ID and ARM remain public even with Private Link: allow these destinations.
resultCriteria: PASS when the connectivity decision (public, proxy, Arc gateway or Private Link) is documented and the required endpoints are allowed and validated (for example, azcmagent check); WARN when the decision exists without validation evidence. TODO until the customer's documentary evidence is recorded.

title: Inbound ports on the agent (SSH/WAC)
what: incomingConnectionsPorts of the agent.
crit: WARN if there are open ports.
steps: Close inbound ports on the agent where SSH/WAC is not used: azcmagent config set incomingconnections.ports "".
how: Keep them open only on machines with approved use (outside Tier 0) and with access through Entra.
resultCriteria: WARN if there are open ports.

title: Agent mode
what: configMode (full/monitor), extensions, and guest configuration enabled.
crit: Informational.
steps: Use monitor mode on machines that only need inventory and monitoring.
how: Full mode for managed servers; monitor mode for sensitive servers where remote execution is not wanted.
resultCriteria: INFO by design (inventory): reports the agent configuration mode (full/monitor) and locally disabled extensions; extension hardening is scored in CHK-23 and CHK-24.

title: Extension allowlist/blocklist
what: extensionsAllowList and extensionsBlockList configured on the agent.
crit: FAIL when at least half of applicable machines accept any extension; WARN when a smaller subset does; PASS when every applicable machine has an allowlist or blocklist.
steps: Define the extension allowlist per profile (for example, AMA, MDE, SQL, Machine Configuration) and apply it with azcmagent or policy.
how: Start with Tier 0 and exposed servers; on the others, at least a blocklist for CustomScript and RunCommand where they are not used.
resultCriteria: FAIL when at least half of applicable machines accept any extension; WARN when a smaller subset does; PASS when every applicable machine has an allowlist or blocklist.

title: Sensitive extensions
what: Windows Admin Center, OpenSSH, Entra login, AD join, Hybrid Worker, and Custom Script.
crit: WARN: review the need and who can use them.
steps: Review each sensitive extension (WAC, OpenSSH, Entra login, Hybrid Worker, Custom Script): keep it only where there is approved use.
how: Remove if there is no owner and no use in the last 90 days.
resultCriteria: PASS when no sensitive extension (script or command execution) is installed on Arc machines; non-PASS when any is installed.

title: Entra access to the OS (SSH/RDP/WAC)
what: Virtual Machine Administrator/User Login and Windows Admin Center Administrator Login.
crit: Informational: validate scope and use of groups.
steps: Restrict Virtual Machine Administrator/User Login and WAC Administrator Login to groups and to the required scope.
how: Administrator sign-in only through a group with PIM.
resultCriteria: INFO by design (inventory): counts Entra ID login/SSH/Windows Admin Center role assignments that reach Arc machines; scope and use of groups are validated with the customer.

title: Run Command and Admin Center per tier
what: Formal usage decision per tier; Tier 0 blocked by default.
crit: Evidence: approved decision and applied control (allowlist/RBAC).
steps: Decide per tier on the use of Run Command and Admin Center and enforce it through the allowlist and RBAC.
how: Tier 0: blocked by default. Others: allowed with auditing and alerting.
resultCriteria: PASS when Run Command and Windows Admin Center use is defined per tier and enforced (disabled or restricted on Tier 0 by allowlist/RBAC); FAIL when they are unrestricted on Tier 0. TODO until the customer's documentary evidence is recorded.

title: Guest configuration (Machine Configuration)
what: guestConfigurationEnabled on the agent.
crit: WARN if disabled (no policy auditing inside the OS).
steps: Enable guest configuration on the agent on machines that must be audited by policy.
how: Disable only if there is a formal decision (for example, monitor mode) and another configuration control.
resultCriteria: WARN if disabled (no policy auditing inside the OS).

title: Failed extensions
what: provisioningState of all extensions.
crit: FAIL if not Succeeded.
steps: Group failures by cause (finding cause column).

Missing OS dependency (Python): the extension message itself (for example MDE.Linux and OS update on Linux) states that Python is missing; install the distribution python3 package and reapply the extension.

Blocked by the allowlist: decide whether the extension goes into the profile allowlist or whether the assignment should be removed (for example, a patch assessment policy or Hybrid Worker pushed to Tier 0); do not leave it permanently failed.
Other causes: fix (network, OS version, conflict), reinstall, and remove orphaned extensions.
how: The allowlist is a security decision per tier: if the service is needed in the tier, include it; if not, remove the assignment at the source (policy or service). Prioritize MDE, AMA, SQL, and patching.
resultCriteria: PASS when every extension on Arc machines is in Succeeded state; non-PASS when any extension is in a failed state.

title: Agent version within support
what: Version of each Connected Machine agent × release date in the release notes, with the age in months on the run date; only versions released in the last 12 months are supported (table of 2026-10-22: latest 1.68, Sep/2026). Includes the 1.61 security floor (published elevation of privilege CVEs).
crit: FAIL if any agent is out of support; WARN if supported but older than 6 months. FAIL also for versions earlier than 1.61.
steps: Update the agent on machines out of support (released more than 12 months before the collection date).
Prioritize machines below 1.61: CVE-2026-26117 and earlier CVEs allow elevation to SYSTEM and use of the machine identity.
Plan updates for those older than 6 months; standardize monthly updates through Update Manager, WSUS, or the package manager.
how: Out of support = mandatory. Between 6 and 12 months = include in the next window.
resultCriteria: PASS when no machine runs an agent below 1.61 (published elevation-of-privilege CVEs) or older than the 12-month support window, and none is supported but more than 6 months old; non-PASS otherwise.

title: Extension versions and automatic upgrade
what: SQL extension and Azure Monitor Agent × 12-month support window (release notes; current SQL target 1.1.3518.465); other extensions × latest version published by Azure in the region (Extension Metadata; fallback: newest in the estate); enableAutomaticUpgrade.
crit: FAIL if the SQL extension or the Azure Monitor Agent is out of support; WARN if any extension is behind the published version (or the newest in the estate) or without automatic upgrade.
steps: Update the SQL extension and the Azure Monitor Agent outside the 12-month window (only versions released in the last year are supported).
Enable automatic extension upgrade and bring outdated extensions in line with the newest version in the fleet.
how: Automatic upgrade is the recommended default; disable it only with a documented reason.
resultCriteria: FAIL if the SQL extension or the Azure Monitor Agent is out of support; WARN if any extension is behind the published version (or the newest in the estate) or without automatic upgrade.

title: Defender for Servers
what: VirtualMachines plan per subscription (tier and subplan).
crit: FAIL if Free.
steps: Enable Defender for Servers (Plan 1 or 2) on the subscription.
how: Plan 2 when you need agentless vulnerability assessment, FIM, and when you would already use Update Manager/Machine Configuration (included). Plan 1 for basic endpoint protection.
resultCriteria: PASS when Defender for Servers (P1 or P2) is enabled in every subscription with Arc machines; non-PASS when any such subscription is on Free.

title: MDE extension deployed through Arc
what: Connected machines without the MDE.Windows/MDE.Linux extension.
crit: WARN if there are machines without the sensor via Arc.
steps: Install the Defender for Endpoint sensor (MDE.Windows/MDE.Linux) on machines without it, through Defender for Cloud.
how: If MDE was already installed by another tool, confirm the onboarding in the Defender portal.
docs: Defender for Endpoint releases (sensor per platform)
resultCriteria: PARTIAL when any connected machine lacks the MDE extension deployed through Arc (this proves only the Arc extension gap; sensor onboarding and health require Defender portal evidence); PASS when every connected machine has it.

title: Defender recommendations
what: Unhealthy assessments on Arc machines, by severity.
crit: FAIL when any Arc recommendation with affected machines has High severity; WARN when recommendations exist only below High; PASS when none affects an Arc machine.
steps: Address High recommendations first, grouping by type (SQL ones usually dominate the volume).
how: Remediate or exempt with justification; a recommendation without an owner becomes a formal exception.
docs: Risk prioritization in Defender for Cloud
Defender for Cloud governance rules (owner and due date)
Resource Graph queries for Defender for Cloud
resultCriteria: FAIL when any Arc recommendation with affected machines has High severity; WARN when recommendations exist only below High; PASS when none affects an Arc machine.

title: SQL Server: Defender for SQL and least privilege
what: Machines with SQL, Defender for SQL plan, SQL extension version/automatic upgrade (least privilege starting with 1.1.2859.223), SQL on a machine associated with Private Link (the data processing service *.<region>.arcdataservices.com does not support Private Link) and SQL on an unsupported OS (earlier than Windows Server 2016).
crit: WARN if any of these cases occur; N/A without SQL.
steps: Enable Defender for SQL in subscriptions with SQL.
Update the SQL extension to a version with least privilege and auto-upgrade.
Review SQL on machines with Private Link (the data processing service does not use Private Link) and SQL on an OS earlier than Windows Server 2016.
how: SQL on an unsupported OS goes into the modernization plan (LEG).
resultCriteria: WARN if any of these cases occur; N/A without SQL.

title: Local accounts and HIMDS GPO
what: Log on as a service right for NT SERVICE\himds; default agent accounts preserved.
crit: Evidence: GPO/local configuration on a sample.
steps: Ensure 'Log on as a service' for NT SERVICE\himds in the GPO and preserve the default agent accounts.
how: Validate on a sample before changing GPOs in production.
resultCriteria: PASS when local administrator membership is controlled and a GPO restricts access to the HIMDS identity endpoint to the authorized local groups; FAIL when unmanaged local administrators exist. TODO until the customer's documentary evidence is recorded.

title: Local collection on a sample (agent and services)
what: azcmagent show, azcmagent check, azcmagent config list, and catalog Windows services on a sample per profile. Includes the agent scheduled tasks (azcmagent) and the GPO deployment task, and the service startup types.
crit: Evidence: outputs attached to the package.
steps: Run azcmagent show, azcmagent check, and azcmagent config list on a sample per profile and attach the output to the package.
Record the agent scheduled tasks and services: Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName azcmagent (daily, SYSTEM) and Get-Service himds, GCArcService, ExtensionService, arcproxy with their startup type.
how: Minimum sample: one machine per network profile and per OS.
resultCriteria: PASS when local collection on the agreed sample (azcmagent show/check and agent services) shows a healthy agent and running services; WARN when deviations are found. TODO until the customer's documentary evidence is recorded.

title: Disconnected or expired machines
what: Status other than Connected and days since the last change.
crit: FAIL if there is Disconnected/Expired. Expired requires a new onboarding; a disconnected machine does not receive policies, patches, or extensions.
steps: Disconnected: check the himds service, network, and proxy (azcmagent check) and reconnect.
Expired (more than 45 days without connection): redo the onboarding.
Decommissioned or migrated: remove the Arc resource to avoid leaving orphans.
how: If the machine no longer exists, remove it. If it exists, reconnect it. Expired always requires new onboarding.
docs: Uninstall the agent and clean up resources
Data, replication and disaster recovery for Arc-enabled servers
resultCriteria: FAIL if there is Disconnected/Expired. Expired requires a new onboarding; a disconnected machine does not receive policies, patches, or extensions.

title: Advisor recommendations
what: Advisor recommendations for Arc machines.
crit: Informational.
steps: Review and address Advisor recommendations for Arc resources.
how: Follow the severity indicated by Advisor.
resultCriteria: INFO by design (not scored): counts Azure Advisor recommendations that target Arc machines.

title: Azure Monitor Agent
what: Connected machines without AMA.
crit: FAIL when no connected machine has AMA; WARN when only part of the connected estate lacks AMA; PASS when all connected machines have AMA.
steps: Deploy AMA to connected machines through Azure Policy (DeployIfNotExists) or DCR.
how: If the machine does not need logs, document it; otherwise, AMA is the standard (MMA was retired).
resultCriteria: FAIL when no connected machine has AMA; WARN when only part of the connected estate lacks AMA; PASS when all connected machines have AMA.

title: DCR association
what: Machines with AMA and no associated Data Collection Rule; DCRs in use and destination workspaces.
crit: WARN: agent installed without collecting data.
steps: Associate a DCR with machines that have AMA (security events, performance, and Syslog according to the profile).
how: AMA without a DCR collects nothing: define DCRs per profile before expanding.
resultCriteria: PARTIAL (assessment blocked) when no connected machine has Azure Monitor Agent; WARN when a machine with AMA has no associated DCR (agent installed without collecting data); PASS when every machine with AMA has a DCR.

title: Microsoft Sentinel and machine coverage
what: Workspaces with Sentinel; DCRs that send data to them (flows), Arc machines covered by those DCRs, retention, and Activity Log export to Sentinel.
crit: FAIL when Sentinel exists in the collected scope but no Arc machine sends events to it; WARN when Sentinel is not found and an external SOC dependency is unresolved; INFO with measured coverage.
steps: Confirm the SOC workspace with Sentinel and connect the security events of the Arc machines.
how: If Sentinel is in another subscription, include it in the collection or record the dependency.
resultCriteria: FAIL when Sentinel exists in the collected scope but no Arc machine sends events to it; WARN when Sentinel is not found and an external SOC dependency is unresolved; INFO with measured coverage.

title: Patch assessment (Update Manager/WSUS)
what: Periodic assessment (AutomaticByPlatform) and pending critical/security patches.
crit: FAIL for pending critical/security patches or a failed patch extension; PARTIAL when assessment/authority is unknown; PASS only with one valid canonical assessment row per connected machine and no pending critical/security patches.
steps: Enable periodic assessment (AutomaticByPlatform) and address pending critical and security patches.
Check the prerequisites: patch extensions install themselves on the first operation; allow the Windows Update endpoints or the configured WSUS server; on Linux, Python 2.7 or later and sudo for root.
how: Periodic assessment is billed outside the benefits (Defender P2, attested SA, WS PAYG, ESU): consider it in REQ-09.
resultCriteria: FAIL for pending critical/security patches or a failed patch extension; PARTIAL when assessment/authority is unknown; PASS only with one valid canonical assessment row per connected machine and no pending critical/security patches.

title: Activity Log export
what: Subscription diagnostic settings to Log Analytics.
crit: FAIL if there is no export (native retention of 90 days).
steps: Create a subscription diagnostic setting that sends the Activity Log to Log Analytics.
how: Without export, native retention is 90 days: insufficient for investigation.
resultCriteria: PASS when the Activity Log is exported to Log Analytics in every subscription in scope; non-PASS when any subscription has no export.

title: Sensitive operations in the period
what: Run Command, extension installation/removal, machine removal, and licenses.
crit: WARN if there are Run Command operations or removals: review author and justification.
steps: Review the author and justification of sensitive operations (Run Command, extensions, removals).
Create alerts for these operations.
how: An operation without a ticket or without a known author must be investigated.
resultCriteria: WARN if there are Run Command operations or removals: review author and justification.

title: Log Analytics retention
what: retentionInDays of the workspaces.
crit: WARN if less than 90 days.
steps: Set the retention of security workspaces to the defined minimum (90 days or more).
how: Retention per table: longer for security, shorter for performance, controlling cost.
resultCriteria: N/A when no workspace receives Arc machine data through a DCR (coverage is resolved in CHK-39/CHK-40); otherwise PASS when every such workspace keeps at least 90 days of retention and WARN when any keeps less.

title: Pilot executed and accepted
what: Representative scope, metrics, and success criteria (30 days recommended).
crit: Evidence: pilot report.
steps: Run a representative pilot with metrics and success criteria (30 days).
how: Without an accepted pilot, do not start waves.
resultCriteria: PASS when a pilot was executed with documented scope and success criteria and was formally accepted; WARN when executed without formal acceptance. TODO until the customer's documentary evidence is recorded.

title: Rollout in waves and rollback
what: Waves with advance, pause, and rollback criteria.
crit: Evidence: approved plan.
steps: Plan waves with criteria for advancing, pausing, and rollback.
how: Proceed only when the metrics of the previous wave are within expectations.
resultCriteria: PASS when rollout waves with entry/exit criteria and a tested rollback procedure are documented; WARN when waves exist without a tested rollback. TODO until the customer's documentary evidence is recorded.

title: Automation method per environment
what: Onboarding (service principal, SCCM/GPO, PowerShell/Ansible), Azure Policy, and Automation per environment.
crit: Evidence: versioned script and method per environment.
steps: Standardize the onboarding and automation method per environment and version the scripts.
how: One official method per environment; avoid manual installation.
resultCriteria: PASS when the onboarding/configuration automation method for each environment (Azure Policy, script, ConfigMgr or IaC) is documented and repeatable; WARN when some environments rely on manual steps. TODO until the customer's documentary evidence is recorded.

title: Individual and at-scale removal
what: Remove extensions, azcmagent disconnect, uninstall the agent, and clean up orphaned resources via Resource Graph.
crit: Evidence: documented procedure.
steps: Document individual removal (extensions, azcmagent disconnect, uninstallation, dependency cleanup) and at-scale removal (Resource Graph + official script with -WhatIf).
On Arc VMs on Azure Local, use only azcmagent disconnect --force-local-only.
how: Machine exists: individual removal. Does not exist or Expired: at-scale deletion after owner approval. Removing orphans avoids cost and false alerts.
docs: Uninstall the agent and clean up resources
resultCriteria: PASS when individual and at-scale removal procedures (agent disconnect, extension and Azure resource cleanup) are documented and tested; WARN when documented but not tested. TODO until the customer's documentary evidence is recorded.

title: Health KPIs and periodic review
what: % Connected, heartbeat, Succeeded extensions, and policy compliance; monthly RBAC/PIM review.
crit: Evidence: dashboard and review cadence.
steps: Publish a dashboard with % Connected, Succeeded extensions, compliance, agent within support, and Secure Score; monthly review.
Review Service Health security advisories monthly (manual: the details require a role above Reader).
how: Use the recommended alerts as the basis for the indicators.
resultCriteria: PASS when health KPIs (connected %, agent version, extension success, compliance) are defined with an owner and a periodic review is evidenced; WARN when KPIs exist without review evidence. TODO until the customer's documentary evidence is recorded.

title: Legacy, end of support, and ESU
what: Windows Server 2008/2012/2012 R2 (2012 ESU ended on 2026-10-13) and Windows Server 2016 (end of support on 2027-01-12; ESU via Arc with agent 1.62+), with the ESU license state.
crit: FAIL if there is 2008/2012/2012 R2 after ESU ends; WARN if there is 2016 without an assigned ESU or with an agent earlier than 1.62.
steps: Windows Server 2012/2012 R2: isolate, monitor, and migrate (no patches since 2026-10-13).
Windows Server 2016: assign the ESU license through Arc before 2027-01-12 and update the agent to 1.62+.
how: ESU for 2016 requires Software Assurance (or Server Subscription); without it, prioritize migration.
resultCriteria: FAIL if there is 2008/2012/2012 R2 after ESU ends; WARN if there is 2016 without an assigned ESU or with an agent earlier than 1.62.

title: Legacy exceptions and exit plan
what: Exception register with owner, timeframe, and compensating controls; unsupported extensions blocked; migration to WS2019+.
crit: Evidence: approved exception register and roadmap.
steps: Record legacy exceptions with owner, timeframe, and compensating controls, and approve the migration roadmap.
how: Every legacy machine needs an exit date.
resultCriteria: PASS when every legacy/end-of-support machine has a recorded exception (owner, compensating controls, ESU status, expiry) and an exit plan; FAIL when legacy machines have no recorded exception. TODO until the customer's documentary evidence is recorded.

title: Cost: billed services and benefits per machine
what: Monthly list-price estimate (USD) per connected server: Defender for Servers P1/P2, Update Manager, Machine Configuration/Change Tracking, and Windows Server PAYG; benefits that offset part of the cost (attested Software Assurance, WS PAYG, ESU via Arc, Defender P2); variable items (Log Analytics, Sentinel).
crit: INFO with the estimate; WARN if any Windows Server pays for Update Manager/Machine Configuration without an attested benefit (opportunity if there is Software Assurance).
steps: Attest Software Assurance on eligible Windows servers (Azure Arc › Azure Benefits - Windows Server).
Review Defender P1 × P2 and the Machine Configuration policies that include Arc servers unnecessarily.
Create a budget and alert in Cost Management by resource group or tag.
how: Attest only with SA or a valid subscription license. If most servers use Update Manager and Machine Configuration, Defender Plan 2 may be worthwhile.
resultCriteria: INFO by design (not scored): list-price estimate of billed Arc services and benefits per connected machine; Log Analytics cost per GB is not estimated.

title: Threats and vulnerabilities (Defender for Cloud)
what: Active security alerts on Arc machines, vulnerabilities (CVE) by reach and severity, and Secure Score by subscription, with the Defender classification itself.
crit: FAIL if there is an active High alert; WARN if there is an active alert or a High/Critical vulnerability; the Secure Score is informational.
steps: Investigate and address active High alerts in Defender for Cloud/XDR (machine, process, user, and timeline).
Prioritize High/Critical vulnerabilities by the number of affected machines and remediate through Update Manager or WSUS.
Track Secure Score in the executive summary and in the monthly review.
how: Severity is the Defender severity. An active alert without an owner is an incident; a vulnerability with no available fix requires an exception with a compensating control.
docs: Resource Graph queries for Defender for Cloud
resultCriteria: FAIL if there is an active High alert; WARN if there is an active alert or a High/Critical vulnerability; PARTIAL when there are no findings but MDE coverage is not confirmed (zero findings is not evidence of no exposure); the Secure Score is informational.

title: Operating system security baseline
what: Assignment and compliance of the Azure compute security baseline (Windows and Linux) through Machine Configuration on each connected machine.
crit: FAIL if a connected machine has no baseline assigned; WARN if a machine is non-compliant; PASS if all are assigned and compliant.
steps: Assign the built-in Azure compute security baseline policy (Windows and Linux) at the management group or subscription of the Arc machines, first in audit mode.
Address non-compliant settings by priority (Critical and Important) and record exceptions with a justification.
For Windows Server 2025, evaluate the customizable baseline (OSConfig) before applying automatic remediation.
how: The baseline is the cloud equivalent of the security GPO: start by auditing, compare with the current GPO and only then remediate. It does not cover LAPS or BitLocker (CHK-60 and CHK-61).
docs: CAF: Arc security, governance and compliance
resultCriteria: FAIL if a connected machine has no baseline assigned; WARN if a machine is non-compliant; PASS if all are assigned and compliant.

title: Local administrators audit
what: Audit of the local Administrators group through Machine Configuration (built-in Administrators group membership policies) on connected Windows machines.
crit: FAIL when no connected Windows machine has the local-administrators audit; WARN for non-compliance when audit coverage exists; INFO when only part of the estate is covered; PASS when all applicable machines are audited and compliant.
steps: Assign the Machine Configuration policy that audits local Administrators group members, with the approved list per profile.
Remove unapproved accounts and groups; a local administrator also controls the agent and can use the machine identity.
how: Whoever is a local administrator controls the agent: treat it as privileged access (CTL-04).
docs: CAF: Arc security, governance and compliance
resultCriteria: FAIL when no connected Windows machine has the local-administrators audit; WARN for non-compliance when audit coverage exists; INFO when only part of the estate is covered; PASS when all applicable machines are audited and compliant.

title: Healthy antivirus and EDR
what: Defender for Cloud endpoint protection recommendations (antimalware, EDR, Defender for Endpoint) and presence of the MDE extension on connected machines.
crit: FAIL if a high or medium severity endpoint protection recommendation has Unhealthy machines; WARN if there is a low severity recommendation or a connected machine without the MDE extension.
steps: Address the Defender for Cloud endpoint protection recommendations (outdated antimalware, missing or failing EDR).
Install or fix Defender for Endpoint on machines without the MDE extension (or confirm onboarding done by another tool).
how: Healthy antivirus and EDR on every connected machine; exceptions only with a recorded compensating control.
docs: Defender for Endpoint releases (sensor per platform)
resultCriteria: PARTIAL when a connected machine lacks the MDE extension (extension absence does not prove sensor absence); otherwise FAIL if a High/Medium endpoint protection recommendation has Unhealthy machines, WARN if a lower-severity one does, and PASS when none does.

title: Insights and telemetry per machine
what: Which data each connected machine sends through Data Collection Rules: performance, VM Insights and dependency map, events/Syslog, security events and Change Tracking.
crit: FAIL when every connected machine lacks both performance and security-event telemetry; WARN when any connected machine is blind; INFO with the telemetry matrix when coverage exists.
steps: Define DCRs per profile: performance and VM Insights (operations), security events (SOC/Sentinel), events or Syslog (troubleshooting) and Change Tracking (change auditing).
Associate the DCRs with machines without telemetry and validate that data arrives in the workspace.
how: A machine without security events is invisible to the SOC; without performance data, invisible to operations. Adjust collection to the ingestion cost.
resultCriteria: FAIL when every connected machine lacks both performance and security-event telemetry; WARN when any connected machine is blind; INFO with the telemetry matrix when coverage exists.

title: Map of Arc capabilities in use
what: Azure Arc capabilities active in the fleet: AMA, MDE, SQL, Change Tracking/FIM, VM Insights, Key Vault, Hybrid Worker, Admin Center, SSH, Entra ID login, Custom Script, periodic patch assessment, Windows Server Management benefits, Hotpatch and ESU.
crit: Informational: shows what is in use and what is available but unused.
steps: Compare capabilities in use with those available: with Software Assurance or WS PAYG, Update Manager, Change Tracking, Machine Configuration, Admin Center, Remote Support, Best Practices Assessment and Site Recovery configuration have no additional cost.
Evaluate Hotpatch on Windows Server 2025 servers (fewer reboots and a shorter exposure window).
Disable extensions without an owner or without use (CHK-24).
how: Each active capability expands what can be done on the server: enable it with an owner, a reason and access control.
resultCriteria: INFO by design (not scored): maps which of the 24 Arc capabilities are in use on at least one machine.

title: Local administrator password (Windows LAPS)
what: Windows LAPS (backed up to Active Directory or Microsoft Entra ID) or an equivalent solution: unique, rotated local administrator password on each server.
crit: Evidence: Windows LAPS policy applied (GPO or Intune) and a sample of servers with a managed password.
steps: Apply Windows LAPS through GPO (backup to Active Directory) or Intune, with rotation and restricted access to the password.
Disable or rename the built-in local administrator where an alternative exists.
how: A repeated local administrator password enables lateral movement between servers and use of the machine identity in Azure.
docs: CAF: Arc security, governance and compliance
resultCriteria: PASS when Windows LAPS manages the local administrator password on every Windows Arc machine (policy and backup evidence); FAIL when a shared or static local administrator password is in use. TODO until the customer's documentary evidence is recorded.

title: System disk encryption (BitLocker/dm-crypt)
what: Encryption of the operating system volume, which protects the Arc agent private key against offline attacks (CAF recommendation).
crit: Evidence: BitLocker/dm-crypt active on the OS volume of Arc machines or a recorded exception.
steps: Enable BitLocker (Windows) or dm-crypt (Linux) on the operating system volume of Arc servers, starting with Tier 0 and physically exposed servers.
Store recovery keys in AD or Entra ID and test recovery.
how: Without encryption, the agent private key can be copied from a disk or backup and used to impersonate the server.
docs: CAF: Arc security, governance and compliance
resultCriteria: PASS when the system disk is encrypted (BitLocker/dm-crypt) with recovery keys escrowed on every machine; WARN when only part of the machines is covered. TODO until the customer's documentary evidence is recorded.

title: Conditional Access and MFA for Azure administrators
what: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policies that require MFA (and, ideally, a compliant device or privileged access workstation) for the Azure portal, CLI and management APIs.
crit: Evidence: Conditional Access policy for Azure management covering the accounts with roles in the Arc scope.
steps: Require MFA through Conditional Access for the Azure management app, with no exceptions for administrative accounts.
For roles that run code on servers (Contributor, Resource Administrator), also require a compliant device or privileged access workstation and activation through PIM.
how: Whoever manages Azure can run code on Arc servers: that person identity is part of the server attack surface.
resultCriteria: PASS when Conditional Access requires MFA for every identity that administers Azure; FAIL when any administrator can manage Azure without MFA. TODO until the customer's documentary evidence is recorded.

title: Defender for Servers per Arc machine
what: Defender for Servers plan read on each Arc machine (resource-level Pricings): tier, subplan, whether it inherits from the subscription, and enabled extensions.
crit: FAIL if any machine has no Defender for Servers (Free); WARN if the machine plan differs from the subscription plan; PASS if all machines inherit the subscription plan.
steps: Enable Defender for Servers on Arc machines with no plan (Free), at the subscription or on the machine itself.

Review machines whose plan differs from the subscription: confirm whether the exception is intentional (for example, P1 for cost) and record the reason; without a reason, remove the machine-level setting so it inherits the subscription plan again.
how: A machine-level plan overrides the subscription plan: a machine can stay on P1 or Free in a P2 subscription without showing in the per-subscription view.
docs: Defender for Servers at resource level
Pricings - Get (Defender for Cloud REST API)
resultCriteria: PASS when every Arc machine has a Defender for Servers plan equal to its subscription plan; WARN when a machine plan differs from the subscription; FAIL when any machine is on Free (no plan).

title: SQL Server: license and usage upload (billing)
what: Per machine with the SQL Server extension: LicenseType set on the extension (PAYG, Paid, LicenseOnly), use of a physical core license (pCore) and pCore licenses in scope, extension state, uploadStatus and time of the last usage upload (timestampUTC), machine status and operating system.
crit: FAIL for a conclusive technical upload/connection/extension condition even when contractual entitlement coverage is PARTIAL; WARN for license metadata mismatches; N/A without the SQL extension.
steps: First fix machines with no usage upload for more than 24 hours or with uploadStatus other than OK: allow outbound HTTPS 443 to dataprocessingservice.<region>.arcdataservices.com and telemetry.<region>.arcdataservices.com, use a proxy without authentication and confirm the Microsoft.AzureArcData provider is registered.
Reconnect SQL machines that are not Connected within 30 days: with PAYG, the subscription expires and use is no longer authorized.

Set the LicenseType of each extension (PAYG, Paid or LicenseOnly) according to the contract; with a physical core license (pCore), set UsePhysicalCoreLicense and align LicenseType with the license billingPlan.
Fix failed extensions and plan to retire Windows Server versions older than 2016, which don't meet the TLS required by the data processing service.
how: The hourly usage upload supports PAYG billing, the reporting of Software Assurance licenses and the detection of passive AG/FCI replicas (billed at USD 0 only when detected).
docs: Licensing and billing of SQL Server enabled by Azure Arc
Connectivity to the SQL Arc data processing service and telemetry
Troubleshoot the SQL Server extension (Azure Arc)
resultCriteria: FAIL for a conclusive technical upload/connection/extension condition even when contractual entitlement coverage is PARTIAL; WARN for license metadata mismatches; N/A without the SQL extension.
